text: Walls lie?
speaker: Kurash

text: People build walls to be believed.
speaker: Zik

text: He rested a hand on the ancient brickwork. Heat stored in the brick pressed steadily into his palm.
speaker: Narrator

text: They repair them. Reface them. Reuse them. Tear them down and build them again.
speaker: Zik

text: He tapped the black mortar.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: But nobody thinks about the mud between the bricks.
speaker: Zik

text: Enhedu nodded slowly.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: So you read the mud.
speaker: Enhedu

text: I read the people who mixed it.
speaker: Zik

text: For a moment no one spoke. The desert wind hissed across the ridge above them, carrying another veil of sand into the excavation. It settled over their boots and against the exposed face of the ruin as though trying to bury it again. Kurash looked back toward the open desert.
speaker: Narrator

text: My uncle always said the old kings hid their treasure because they feared thieves.
speaker: Kurash

text: Balag snorted.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The old kings were the thieves.
speaker: Balag

text: I suppose that's true.
speaker: Kurash

text: So why bury it at all?
speaker: Kurash

text: Zik's eyes stayed on the wall. The pattern of replacements held his attention even while he answered.
speaker: Narrator

text: Maybe it wasn't treasure they wanted hidden.
speaker: Zik

text: Enhedu followed his gaze.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: What, then?
speaker: Enhedu

text: I don't know.
speaker: Zik

text: He brushed one last ribbon of sand from the black mortar.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: But whatever this place was built to keep…
speaker: Zik
note: Let the warning land. Slow slightly.

text: His fingers paused against the glassy seam.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: …someone came back long after it was finished and decided it still wasn't safe enough.
speaker: Zik
note: Let the warning land. Slow slightly.

text: No one joked after that.
speaker: Narrator

text: Clear it,
speaker: Zik

text: Zik said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: They dug until the sun started its slow drop toward the west. Sand slid back into the hole as fast as they pulled it out. The deeper they went, the colder the air turned. A draft rose out of the dark and touched Zik's face. It smelled of dry earth. Under that was something that had never met the sun.
speaker: Narrator

text: The stairway went farther down than the structure above had any right to allow. Walls narrowed until they walked single file. Balag took the lead because he was largest and apparently considered it his job to find whatever killed them first. Enhedu came next. Zik followed. Kurash brought up the rear and complained under his breath every time the steps grew steeper. Zik paid him no mind. He listened.
speaker: Narrator

text: The deeper they went, the quieter the surface became. Wind and shifting sand faded first. Then the voices of the men working above. Then the faint creak of the rope they had used to secure the entrance. The stairway did not carry sound. It took it. Balag stopped without warning. Zik nearly walked into him.
speaker: Narrator

text: What?
speaker: Enhedu

text: Enhedu kept her voice low.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Balag raised one hand. For several long breaths nothing moved in the dark past the reach of the torch. Then, far below, a sound reached them—not a knock, not stone scraping stone, but a low vibration, as if something massive had shifted its weight under a great thickness of rock. Balag touched two fingers to his chest in the old ward his grandfather had taught him. Zik had seen the gesture before, always when Balag thought no one watched.
speaker: Narrator

text: You believe in that now?
speaker: Enhedu

text: Enhedu asked.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I believe in not insulting whatever sits under this much earth.
speaker: Balag

text: Specific religion.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Keep talking. I'll convert you.
speaker: Balag

text: They went on. At the bottom stood a stone door set so clean into the wall that the seam nearly vanished. Heavy bronze brackets held it shut from the outside. Age had darkened the metal but left it free of corrosion. Each bracket carried the same mark: a jagged spiral closed around a single drop. Zik had only seen that symbol on private royal seals, the kind belonging to kings whose reigns ended briefly, violently, and with their names scrubbed from most records. He crouched beside the nearest bracket.
speaker: Narrator

text: How old?
speaker: Balag

text: Balag asked.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Older than the door.
speaker: Zik

text: Not helpful.
speaker: Balag

text: Wasn't trying to be.
speaker: Zik

text: Enhedu stepped up beside him. Her eyes moved across the bronze, the stone, the symbol.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Whatever's inside wasn't trying to leave.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Zik considered the brackets.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Someone worked hard to keep it there.
speaker: Zik

text: Enhedu's smile returned, slow and sharp.
speaker: Narrator
